source: https://github.com/garvitkhurana/mlx-voice-clone (repo root)

claim: Local voice-cloned text-to-speech on macOS, built on mlx-audio + Qwen3
source: README.md:3 "Local **voice-cloned TTS** on macOS (Apple Silicon) via [mlx-audio](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio) + Qwen3."

claim: Runs locally on an Apple Silicon Mac using MLX (Apple's on-device ML framework), not a cloud API
source: README.md:9 "macOS + Apple Silicon" and scripts/qwen3_clone.py:3-4 "Minimal Qwen3-TTS voice clone on Apple Silicon (MLX). Requires: macOS + Apple Silicon"

claim: Network is needed only on first run to download the Hugging Face model; after that generation is local (no cloud API call, no per-use bill)
source: README.md:12 "Network on first run (Hugging Face model download)"

claim: Model weights are identified by fixed Hugging Face repo IDs and loaded once per run via load_model, so after the first download they are cached and reused from local disk rather than re-fetched
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:32-33 "MODEL_LITE = \"mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base-8bit\"" / "MODEL_PRO = \"mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-8bit\""; qwen3_clone.py:571-572 "Load once so chunked runs do not repeatedly fetch/initialize. loaded_model = load_model(model_id)"

claim: Three inputs drive a clone: a reference voice clip, the exact transcript of what was said in that clip, and the script to narrate
source: README.md:24-27 "--ref-audio ./sample_clip.m4a --ref-text-file documents/ref_voice_transcript.txt --text-file documents/01_intro.txt"

claim: Supplying the reference clip's exact transcript (--ref-text-file) skips Whisper transcription of the clip, which is faster and repeatable
source: README.md:70 "**`--ref-text-file`** skips Whisper on the reference clip (faster, repeatable)."

claim: If no reference transcript is given, the tool transcribes the reference clip itself with Whisper (an extra model download and slower)
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:405-407 "If omitted, mlx-audio transcribes with Whisper (extra model download + slower)."

claim: Running example: the repo's own reference clip and transcript (candidate for the video's running example) — a ~15-20s clip where the speaker introduces themself and their work
source: documents/ref_voice_transcript.txt (full text) "Hi, I'm Garvit Khurana. This is a short reference clip for local voice cloning on my Mac. I work on AI products for capital markets, and I use this tool to narrate scripts in my own voice."

claim: Running example: the demo narration script the repo ships to be spoken in the cloned voice
source: documents/01_intro.txt "Hey!\nI'm Garvit Khurana — nice to meet you."

claim: Long scripts are split into pieces at paragraph/sentence boundaries under a character limit (default 700, README example uses 450), each piece is synthesized separately, then the pieces are joined into one output file
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:478-481 "--chunk-chars ... default=700 ... Chunk long text into this many chars per pass"; qwen3_clone.py:146-186 _split_long_text() splits on paragraph/sentence boundaries

claim: Chunks are joined end to end with no overlap and no crossfade: ffmpeg's concat demuxer with stream copy (-c copy) does a hard splice, not a blended merge
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:360-390 _concat_wavs(): "Concatenate WAV parts losslessly via ffmpeg concat demuxer" using -f concat -safe 0 ... -c copy (no filter/crossfade applied)

claim: Chunking exists because the underlying generator truncates long text: the default token cap in mlx-audio (1200) would cut off a long script if run in a single pass, so this tool raises the cap and also splits into pieces
unit: tokens (mlx-audio default max_tokens, before this tool's override)
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:472-475 "--max-tokens ... default=4096 ... Token cap for generation (mlx-audio default 1200 truncates long scripts)."

claim: The browser UI is a thin wrapper that runs the same CLI script as a subprocess and streams its logs to the page; it does not reimplement synthesis
source: README.md:57 "`scripts/tts_ui_server.py` | Thin wrapper: runs the CLI as a subprocess, streams logs"; scripts/tts_ui_server.py:276-329 _build_qwen_cmd() builds the same `qwen3_clone.py` CLI invocation, _stream_generate() runs it via subprocess.Popen and yields each stdout line as an SSE event

claim: The browser UI shows live progress by streaming the CLI's stdout/stderr lines to the page over Server-Sent Events (SSE) as generation runs, chunk by chunk
source: scripts/tts_ui_server.py:308-329 _stream_generate(): "for line in proc.stdout: ... yield f\"data: {json.dumps({'log': line})}\\n\\n\""; qwen3_clone.py:602-603 prints "Generating chunk {i}/{len(chunks)}..." per chunk

claim: Two quality modes trade size for speed vs fidelity: lite uses a 0.6B-parameter model for faster iteration, pro uses a 1.7B-parameter model when quality matters more
source: README.md:73 "**Quality:** `lite` (0.6B) for iteration, `pro` (1.7B) when you care about quality."; qwen3_clone.py:32-33 model IDs "Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base-8bit" / "Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-8bit"

claim: Default quality mode is lite unless --quality pro is passed
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:426-431 "--quality choices=('lite','pro') default='lite'"

claim: A --speed flag controls speaking rate directly during synthesis (1.0 = model default, greater than 1 is faster); default is 1.08, about 8% quicker than the model's natural pace
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:449-454 "--speed ... default=1.08 ... Speaking rate (1.0 = model default, >1 faster). Default: 1.08 (~8%% quicker)."

claim: Speaking speed is separate from pitch: pitch is not adjustable in this tool and must be changed afterward by editing the exported audio file externally
source: README.md:102 "**Pitch** (separate from speaking speed): edit the exported file externally without re-synthesizing."

claim: Default output file format is AAC-encoded .m4a (produced via ffmpeg from an intermediate WAV); raw WAV can be requested instead
source: README.md:74 "**Export:** default AAC `.m4a` via ffmpeg. Raw WAV: `--output-format wav`."; qwen3_clone.py:513-518 "--output-format choices=('m4a','wav') default='m4a'"

claim: Reference audio is converted to 24 kHz mono before synthesis, and generated speech is produced at 24 kHz
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:30 "SAMPLE_RATE = 24_000"; README.md:71 "Ref audio is converted to **24 kHz mono WAV**"

claim: Generated files are named with the time of generation plus the script's filename stem
source: README.md:60 "**Output naming:** `HHMMSS_<script_stem>.m4a`"

claim: ffmpeg must be installed and on PATH (used to convert reference audio, export final audio, and concatenate chunked output); the tool errors with an install hint if it is missing
source: README.md:11 "`ffmpeg` on `PATH` (`brew install ffmpeg`)"; scripts/qwen3_clone.py:85-88 "raise RuntimeError('ffmpeg not found. Install with: brew install ffmpeg')"

claim: uv (or Python 3.12+) is required to install dependencies and run the scripts
source: README.md:10 "[uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) (or Python 3.12+)"

claim: The converted 24 kHz mono reference WAV is cached on disk keyed by the source file's path, size and modified time, so repeated runs with the same clip skip re-conversion
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:36-65 _ref_cache_key() and _ensure_wav(): cache_dir keyed by "src.resolve().as_posix()|size|mtime", reused if "out.is_file()"

claim: Levers that change generation speed: lite vs pro model, chunk size, --fast (fewer, larger chunks, each needing one reference re-encode), reference-text file (skips Whisper), and the reference-audio cache; the UI itself does not make the model faster
source: README.md:84 "Speed levers: `lite` vs `pro`, chunk size, `--fast`, ref text file, and cache. The UI does not make the model faster."; qwen3_clone.py:489-493 "--fast ... Fewer ICL passes: enforce a higher chunk floor (~900 chars) for voice-clone mode (each chunk runs a full reference encode; fewer chunks = faster)."

claim: After generation, stderr reports playback length (how long the output sounds) separately from generation wall-clock time (how long the Mac took to produce it) so the two are not confused
source: scripts/qwen3_clone.py:288-299 "Stats: playback length (how long it sounds): ... Stats: generation time (wall clock on this Mac, model+synth+export): ... not the same as playback length above"
